title: MATE: Switch times from floats to doubles
description:
Floats are not wide enough to store relative time stamps.
They really should be nstime_t and FT_RELATIVE_TIME, but doubles
and FT_DOUBLE is better.

Fix #19864.

notes.body:
Is this a potential "breaking change" that should be noted in the release notes?  
If there are display filters that used the MATE attributes based on the float time formatting???

I'd expect it to be breaking only for filters that test a MATE attribute whose value changes as a result of the increased precision.  An == or != test is probably unwise for most numerical values, as you might not be able to represent the numerical value in binary.  Order tests might work OK, as, if you're expecting not to have any packets miscategorized, you probably shouldn't.

(A future change to `FT_RELATIVE_TIME` would avoid those issues, as it's binary seconds and binary nanoseconds, both of which are integers and thus not subject to "doesn't work in binary" issues.)
Not part of your change, but "transport"

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/15887/diffs?diff_id=1030810014&start_sha=bb361138e9d1a1317b6b8690f4e667bc93cfb36f#8ac083e6e425877323c19a4a0116d8fb304a9172_816_816)
Sure, might as well fix that too.
Yeah, that was me anxiously checking the pipeline to make sure the check I added isn't causing grief..

> An == or != test is probably unwise for most numerical values, as you might not be able to represent the numerical value in binary.

Yes, as noted in #16483, floating point comparisons are difficult and unreliable.
